thread.title: SENIOR SPOTLIGHT: Taylor Gibson - NewsBreak

author: J.W. COOKE Keys
title: SENIOR SPOTLIGHT: Taylor Gibson - NewsBreak
text:
By J.W. COOKE Keys ,
5 hours ago Q: How long have you been playing lacrosse?
A: I started lacrosse when I was 5 years old.
Q: Did you ever play any other sports growing up?
A: Growing up, I was on the swim team, gymnastics, sailing, dance, soccer, and lacrosse.
Q: Why not stick to those sports and just focus on lacrosse in high school?
A: Because is something I’ve enjoyed playing my entire life, and I joined Colorguard because I did baton in eighth grade and I wanted to continue performing in high school. I stopped doing swim, my junior and senior years, because of a ruptured eardrum that kept me out during my junior year.
Q: How does your training differ when you are in the season compared to the offseason?
A: My training out of season is slower, but I try my best to keep up with my sports and practice off-season
Q: Do you have downtime away from sports?
A: No
Q: Rating the sports you play versus academics, which is more important in your life?
A: Academics are very important in my life, but to my mental state, sports are my life and always will be. They keep me going even when everything else gets hard.
Q: Between color guard and lacrosse, which sport is most important?
A: Both color guard and lacrosse are equally important to me, but I’m going to college for lacrosse.
Q: Besides sports, are there any ways you are uniquely gifted?
A: I love to surf and have gained skills very quickly in it.
Q: What skills do sports teach you that you apply to life?
A: To work as a team and not get frustrated even when times are hard
Q: What goals do you have for your senior year, academically and/or athletically?
A: I just got all superior at states for color guard, and that was such a big accomplishment for me. For lacrosse, I’m really hoping we win districts and go on to regionals.
Q: What are your personal dreams?
A: I wanna go to college for marine biology and lacrosse. And then after college, I want to move to Costa Rica for research and to live there.
Q: What has been your best high school sports moment?
A: My best moment was last year, January 22, 2025. It was the anniversary of my dad’s passing three years ago, and I was able to make a goal at our game in honor of him, and the whole team cheered for me.
Q: Any coaches, teachers, or family members who have helped you reach this point?
A: I want to thank my mom for supporting me and coming to all my games, and I wanted to thank my dad, even though he’s not with us, for being the voice in my head telling me to keep going even when times are hard.
Q: What advice would you give to the next generation of Conchs?
A: I really want to encourage everyone to show up every day with a positive attitude and to not discourage each other when times are hard. Showing up means you care for the sport, and it shows your teammates and your coaches that you wanna win, and it helps build team connections as well. Show up positive and ready to train.
Q: What is the best advice you’ve received?
A: The best of vice I received was from my coach, Coach G, and she told us that you should use lacrosse as an outlet from your everyday life when it’s hard or even when it’s happy, that you come out to practice and leave everything on the field. Let practice help your worries and to get your mind off of everything.
Q: Having invested so much time — physically, mentally, and emotionally — in your sports, how can you have proper closure during your senior year?
A: Nothing will ever make leaving high school easy. I’m just happy and grateful that I’m spending these last moments with my team and that I’m creating memories that are gonna last me a lifetime.
Q: Anywhere in the world you want to visit?
A: During college, I really want to study abroad to do marine biology work. I want to be anywhere and everywhere that’s on the water, helping the environment and the animals.
Q: Do you have any hobbies outside of sports?
A: Some hobbies I like to do are painting, driving around, going to the jumping bridge, spending time with my friends, and traveling.
Q: What are some challenges you’ve faced as a student-athlete?
A: The biggest challenge I faced was my freshman year. I broke my back during swim. I broke my lower L3 disc, and I wasn’t able to play lacrosse my freshman year.
Q: If you could add one hour to your day, what would you do with it?
A: I would use it to sleep in in the morning, or spend an hour going out after school.
Q: What are your plans for after high school?
A: After high school, I’m gonna be attending Flagler University and playing lacrosse for them, I’m also gonna be joining the surfing team
Q: If you have an opportunity to play a sport in college, no matter the size or location of the school, will you take it?
A: Absolutely.
Q: What would you tell your college roommate about the Keys?
A: I would tell my roommate that it is a beautiful place to visit, but you’re gonna miss shopping and having a lot of things to do.
Q: On your first trip back home, what will be the meal you ask for?
A: When I come home from college, I’m gonna ask my mom to make my favorite pierogies and grilled onions.
Q: Do you have any career aspirations?
A: I’m planning on becoming a marine biologist working with sharks and other marine animals.
